newsitem.title: UK: UK to proceed with Housing Association loans sale.
newsitem.headline: UK to proceed with Housing Association loans sale.

text.p: The British government has decided to proceed with the sale of a 1.1 billion stg loan portfolio of the Housing Corporation and its Scottish and Welsh equivalents, Environment Secretary John Gummer said on Thursday.
The government announced a decision in principle to sell the loans in November last year, and later appointed N and M Rothschilds as its financial advisers for the project.

"On the basis of Rothschilds' advice, the Secretaries of State for Scotland and Wales and I have decided to proceed with the sale of the loans, subject to receiving satisfactory final bids at the conclusion of negotiations," Gummer said in a written parliamentary answer.
He said there had already been "considerable interest" from the private sector, adding: "I expect a successful conclusion to the sale negotiations."
"Housing associations have been most successful in securing private resources to finance social housing projects," Gummer said.
"The sale of the loan portfolios will be the logical conclusion of our policy of withdrawing from a lending activity which can clearly be funded directly by the private sector."

Gummer gave no indication of when the sales would be completed, although he said that for technical reasons, the sale of Scottish Homes loans would take longer than those of the Housing Corporation and Housing for Wales.
